maya: Heads up — after driver 56321 rolled into staging we started seeing selector oscillation on the short-seq hotpath (seq <= 128). latency spikes and kv-cache mispredictions.
jonathan: Ugh. Repro steps?
maya: Quick repro in staging: run the 64/1 throughput test (our small-batch chat load). Profiling shows kernel flip between fast_attn_v2 and slowpath_fold every ~200ms.
sara: Any change in batcher behavior or kv-prefetch windows after the driver bump?
maya: Yes — telemetry shows kv-prefetch window shrank (we think memory allocator changed timings). Combined with autotuner scoring, it flips tie-breaks and we get the slower kernel selected under identical inputs.
lin: Can you paste the perf snippet?
maya: ```
perf trace:
seq=64 batch=1 model=tiny-llm
  t0 kernel=fast_attn_v2 lat=8.3ms
  t1 kernel=slowpath_fold lat=13.7ms
  t2 kernel=fast_attn_v2 lat=8.1ms
  t3 kernel=slowpath_fold lat=14.2ms
kv_prefetch: hit_rate drops from 0.98 -> 0.66 during oscillation
```
alex: That hit_rate drop explains token-latency variance. If kv cache prefetch misses, slowpath wins because it avoids certain memory patterns.
jonathan: Do we see this on dedicated pools or only hosted staging?
maya: Both, but much more visible when the host driver is 56321. Older driver baseline 560xx is stable.
sara: Options: 1) rollback driver in staging, 2) force kernel override for short seq, 3) adjust autotuner tie-break weights, 4) change kv-prefetch thresholds to be less aggressive.
lin: For rollback we need change window with infra — how long to test? We should have a canary rollback in eu-west-1 for 2 hours.
alex: Kernel override for short-term is low-risk. We can patch selector config to prefer fast_attn_v2 when seq<=128 and batch<=2.
jonathan: Can we do a darkroll first? Toggle in runtime flags for 5% of traffic and watch latency & kv hit metrics.
maya: I pushed a trial config to canary with 5% routed: ```
routing.rule: canary_proportion: 0.05
kernel_selector.override:
  condition: "seq <= 128 && batch_size <= 2"
  prefer: fast_attn_v2
```
ops-bot: deploy-started canary/staging 2409876601 by maya
ci-bot: perf-smoke passed on canary (baseline vs override): p50 -1.2ms, p95 -7.5ms, kv_hit +0.12
sara: Good. If canary looks stable, we can escalate to 50% then full. Meanwhile infra should prepare driver rollback plan as contingency.
lin: Rollback plan draft: - coordinate with infra to pin driver to 56048 on affected pools - run 1h soak, run autotune reindex, then promote. If autopick behavior returns to baseline, signal ops to lift kernel overrides.
jonathan: Also add an autotuner guard: when driver version != verified list, increase tie-breaker epsilon so selection is stable.
alex: Agree — small change in scoring formula: add driver_version factor and reduce sensitivity to minor latency deltas.
maya: I'll open a short RFC and a changelist with three patches: canary override, autotuner epsilon, and rollback runbook.
sara: Timeline? We should aim to have canary -> 50% by EOD and rollback PR ready if canary fails.
maya: On it. I'll post results in this thread. Thanks!
ops-bot: deploy-success canary/staging 2409876688 by maya
ci-bot: telemetry-alert: canary latency variance down 60%, kv_hit restored to 0.95
jonathan: Nice. Keep monitoring for 24h; if anything pops, we fallback to rollback plan.
maya: Will do — I'll collect flamegraphs and attach after 2h soak.
alex: One more note: capture kernel selection seeds for the autotuner so we can reproduce deterministic picks across driver versions.
maya: Added to the RFC checklist."
